english.notes:
(i) This offence wording should be used where the offender has simply failed to answer his bail to court or a police station (not to be confused with breach of a bail condition which is not an offence).
(ii) Where the offender has a reasonable cause for not answering his bail and then failed to surrender as soon as practicable see associated offence wording at H567.
(iii) Where the circumstances are such that there has been a breach of bail conditions see offence wording H4240.
(iv) Section 15(3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 amends the six month time limit on prosecution for this offence. The time limit for prosecution is now six months or three months from the first of the following events:- the person surrenders to custody; the person is arrested or attends at a police station in connection with the relevant offence or the offence for which he is granted bail; or the person appears or is brought before a court in connection with the relevant offence or the offence for which he was granted bail.
(v) There is a specific power of arrest under section 46A of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984, for persons who have failed to surrender to custody at a police station.

other.powersofarrest:
A power of arrest is provided by section 7 of the the Bail Act 1976 and may be employed to prevent an individual breaking his bail to court. (Where an individual has failed to attend at court, application should be made for an arrest warrant).
Specific instructions regarding the court to which the offender must be returned are shown at Notes(i) and (ii) below.

"A person who has been released on bail in criminal proceedings and is under a duty to surrender into the custody of a court may be arrested without a warrant by a constable:-
(i) if a constable has reasonable grounds for believing that that person is not likely to surrender to custody;
(ii) if the constable has reasonable grounds for believing that that person is likely to break any of the conditions of his bail or has reasonable grounds for suspecting that person has broken any of those conditions; or
(iii) in a case where that person was released on bail with one or more surety or sureties if a surety notifies a constable in writing that that person is unlikely to surrender to custody and that for that reason the surety wishes to be relieved of his obligation as a surety." (section 7).
other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

If committed for sentence by the Crown Court or following contempt proceedings:
Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
